brdSummary.businessObjective: Provide a self-service portal enabling new hires to complete onboarding tasks (profile, documents, equipment, training) while giving HR oversight and control over the process.
keyCapabilities: SSO-based new hire login and onboarding checklist
Equipment request approval and IT provisioning workflow
HR tracking of completion status and reminders
Automated welcome pack email and audit logging
Role-based access across four user roles
Integrations with Azure AD, email service, and HRIS

requirementInventory.text: New hires can log in with SSO.
New hires can see a checklist of onboarding tasks with due dates.
New hires upload identity documents (PDF/JPG, max 5MB).
New hires upload tax documents (PDF/JPG, max 5MB).
HR is notified on document upload.
IT provisions accounts on approval of equipment requests.
HR can track completion status across all new hires.
HR can send reminders to new hires.
The system emails a welcome pack.
The system logs all actions for audit.
System supports four user roles: New Hire, HR Coordinator, IT Admin, Manager.
Integration with Azure AD for SSO.
Integration with HRIS for employee records.
System must handle 200 concurrent new hires.

epics.description: SSO login for new hires and role-based access control across all four user roles.
epics.businessValue: Ensures secure, seamless access and appropriate permission boundaries for each role.

epics.description: Checklist of onboarding tasks with due dates visible to new hires.
epics.businessValue: Gives new hires clarity on required onboarding steps and deadlines, reducing HR follow-up burden.

epics.description: Upload of identity and tax documents with validation, secure storage, and HR notification.
epics.businessValue: Streamlines compliance document collection and ensures HR visibility into submissions.

epics.description: Manager approval of equipment requests and subsequent IT account provisioning.
epics.businessValue: Automates cross-team handoff between Manager and IT ensuring new hires are equipped on day one.

epics.description: HR tracking of completion status, sending reminders, and automated welcome pack emails.
epics.businessValue: Provides HR with visibility and tools to drive onboarding completion and communicate with new hires.

epics.description: System-wide action logging and audit trail capability.
epics.businessValue: Supports compliance and traceability of all onboarding actions.

epics.description: Integrations with Azure AD, email service, and HRIS for employee records.
epics.businessValue: Ensures data consistency and reduces manual duplication across enterprise systems.

epics.description: Scalability to support 200 concurrent new hires and other non-functional platform qualities.
epics.businessValue: Ensures the platform performs reliably during peak onboarding periods (e.g., new hire cohorts).

stories.storyTitle: IT Account Provisioning on Equipment Approval
stories.userStory: As an IT Admin, I want accounts to be provisioned automatically when a manager approves an equipment request, so that new hires receive the necessary system access without manual tracking.
stories.description: When a Manager approves an equipment request submitted for a new hire, IT provisions the corresponding accounts. This story covers the trigger (equipment approval) and the resulting provisioning action visible/actionable to IT Admin.

acceptanceCriteria.criteria: Given a Manager has an equipment request pending for a new hire, when the Manager approves the request, then IT is triggered to provision the account(s) associated with that request.
Given an equipment request has not been approved, when IT views provisioning tasks, then no provisioning action is available/triggered for that request.
Given a Manager rejects an equipment request, when the rejection is recorded, then no account provisioning is triggered.
Given an equipment request is approved, when provisioning is triggered, then IT Admin can view the provisioning task tied to that specific new hire and request.
Given only a Manager role can approve equipment requests, when a non-Manager attempts to approve, then the approval is not permitted and provisioning is not triggered.

testCases.scenario: Manager approves equipment request, IT provisioning triggered
steps: Manager logs in
Manager opens pending equipment request
Manager approves request
testCases.expectedResult: Provisioning task created/visible for IT Admin

steps: Create equipment request
Leave request in pending state
Check IT provisioning queue
testCases.expectedResult: No provisioning task exists for the pending request

testCases.scenario: Rejected equipment request does not provision account
steps: Manager opens equipment request
Manager rejects request
Check IT provisioning queue
testCases.expectedResult: No provisioning task created

testCases.scenario: IT Admin views specific provisioning task after approval
steps: Approve equipment request for new hire X
IT Admin opens provisioning task list
testCases.expectedResult: Task tied to new hire X is visible with correct request reference

testCases.scenario: Unauthorized role attempts approval
steps: Log in as New Hire or IT Admin
Attempt to approve an equipment request
testCases.expectedResult: Approval action is blocked/unavailable; no provisioning triggered

testCases.scenario: Duplicate approval action on same request does not duplicate provisioning
steps: Manager approves request
Attempt to approve the same already-approved request again
testCases.expectedResult: System does not trigger a second provisioning task for the same request

testCases.scenario: Account provisioning triggered exactly at the moment of manager approval action
steps: Manager opens equipment request in pending state
Manager clicks approve action
Observe system state immediately at approval commit
testCases.expectedResult: Account provisioning process is triggered exactly once at the point approval is recorded, not before or after

testCases.scenario: Provisioning for the last equipment request in a batch of multiple pending approvals
steps: Create multiple equipment requests for different new hires
Approve all requests in sequence
Verify provisioning for the final request in the sequence
testCases.expectedResult: Each approval independently triggers provisioning, including the last item in the batch, with no missed or duplicated provisioning

testCases.scenario: Approval and provisioning at day boundary (e.g., 23:59:59 to 00:00:00)
steps: Set system clock near midnight boundary
Manager approves equipment request just before midnight
Verify provisioning timestamp and account creation date
testCases.expectedResult: Provisioning occurs correctly regardless of date/time boundary crossing, with accurate timestamp recorded

testCases.scenario: Single equipment request containing the minimum allowed equipment item count triggers provisioning
steps: Create equipment request with the minimum permitted number of items (e.g., 1 item)
Manager approves the request
Verify account provisioning occurs
testCases.expectedResult: Provisioning is triggered correctly even for the smallest valid equipment request

testCases.scenario: Provisioning at maximum allowed equipment items in a single request
steps: Create equipment request with maximum allowed number of equipment items
Manager approves the request
Verify provisioning completes for all associated access needs
testCases.expectedResult: Provisioning completes successfully for the maximum boundary equipment request size

dependencies: Is blocked by S-007 (Additional requirements (R-001–R-013)): Provisioning is triggered by manager approval of an equipment request; the request flow and the Manager/IT Admin roles come from the foundation story.
Is blocked by S-005 (System-Wide Audit Logging of Actions): Approval and provisioning actions must be recorded in the audit trail (R-011), so logging must exist first to avoid rework.
Relates to EXT-ITSM (IT provisioning target systems / service desk): Actual account creation depends on the downstream IT systems the provisioning task hands off to.

stories.storyTitle: HR Dashboard for Onboarding Completion Tracking
stories.userStory: As an HR Coordinator, I want to track onboarding completion status across all new hires, so that I can oversee progress and identify who needs attention.
stories.description: HR Coordinator views a consolidated view of completion status of onboarding tasks (profile, documents, equipment, training) for all new hires currently in the portal.

acceptanceCriteria.criteria: Given multiple new hires exist in the system, when an HR Coordinator opens the tracking view, then completion status for each new hire's onboarding tasks is displayed.
Given a new hire has completed all onboarding tasks, when HR views that new hire's status, then it is shown as complete.
Given a new hire has incomplete tasks, when HR views that new hire's status, then the incomplete items are indicated.
Given a user is not HR, when that user attempts to access the completion tracking view, then access is not permitted.
Given no new hires exist yet, when HR opens the tracking view, then an empty state is shown with no errors.

testCases.expectedResult: Status for every new hire is listed

steps: Select new hire with all tasks done

testCases.expectedResult: Status marked complete

testCases.scenario: Partially completed new hire shows incomplete items
steps: Select new hire with some tasks pending
View status
testCases.expectedResult: Pending tasks are indicated distinctly from completed ones

testCases.scenario: Non-HR role attempts to access dashboard
steps: Log in as New Hire
Attempt to navigate to HR tracking dashboard URL/feature
testCases.expectedResult: Access denied

steps: Ensure no new hires in system

testCases.expectedResult: Dashboard renders without error, indicating no records

steps: Ensure no new hire records exist in the system

testCases.expectedResult: Dashboard shows an empty state with zero new hires, no errors

testCases.scenario: Dashboard displays exactly one new hire record
steps: Create exactly one new hire record with partial onboarding completion
HR Coordinator opens the dashboard
testCases.expectedResult: Dashboard correctly displays the single new hire's completion status

steps: Create new hire record with no tasks completed
View dashboard status for this new hire
testCases.expectedResult: Status correctly reflects 0% completion

testCases.scenario: New hire at exactly 100% onboarding completion
steps: Create new hire record with all onboarding tasks marked complete
View dashboard status for this new hire
testCases.expectedResult: Status correctly reflects 100% completion

testCases.scenario: Dashboard displays the maximum number of new hire records supported
steps: Populate system with the maximum supported number of new hire records
HR Coordinator opens the dashboard
testCases.expectedResult: Dashboard loads and displays all records without truncation or errors at the upper limit

dependencies: Is blocked by S-007 (Additional requirements (R-001–R-013)): The dashboard aggregates checklist completion and document upload status, which are produced by the foundation story.
Is blocked by S-008 (Additional requirements (R-015–R-019)): Dashboard access must be restricted to the HR Coordinator role, which requires RBAC enforcement.
Relates to S-005 (System-Wide Audit Logging of Actions): Dashboard views and exports of new-hire data are auditable actions.

stories.storyTitle: HR Send Reminders to New Hires
stories.userStory: As an HR Coordinator, I want to send reminders to new hires, so that they complete outstanding onboarding tasks.
stories.description: HR Coordinator can trigger a reminder to one or more new hires regarding their onboarding tasks.

acceptanceCriteria.criteria: Given an HR Coordinator selects a new hire, when they choose to send a reminder, then a reminder is sent to that new hire.
Given a non-HR user, when they attempt to send a reminder, then the action is not permitted.
Given no new hire is selected, when HR attempts to send a reminder, then the system does not send a reminder without a valid recipient.

dependencies: Is blocked by S-006 (Email Service Integration): Reminders are delivered through the shared email service integration.

Relates to S-002 (HR Dashboard for Onboarding Completion Tracking): Reminder targets are selected from the HR completion-tracking view.
Relates to S-005 (System-Wide Audit Logging of Actions): Each reminder sent must be written to the audit trail.

stories.userStory: As a New Hire, I want to receive a welcome pack email, so that I have introductory onboarding information.
stories.description: The system emails a welcome pack. This story covers the system triggering and sending this welcome email.

acceptanceCriteria.criteria: Given a new hire is onboarded into the system, when the onboarding process is initiated, then the system emails a welcome pack to the new hire.
Given the welcome pack email is sent, when it is delivered, then it is sent to the new hire's registered email address.
Given the email service is unavailable, when the system attempts to send the welcome pack, then the email is not sent and the failure is not silently treated as success.

dependencies: Is blocked by S-006 (Email Service Integration): The welcome pack is delivered through the shared email service integration.

stories.userStory: As an HR Coordinator (or authorized auditor), I want all actions in the system logged, so that there is an audit trail for compliance purposes.
stories.description: The system logs all actions performed within the portal (e.g., document uploads, approvals, provisioning, reminders, status changes) to support an audit trail capability.

acceptanceCriteria.criteria: Given any action is performed in the system (e.g., upload, approval, provisioning, reminder sent), when the action completes, then it is recorded in the audit log.
Given an audit log entry is created, when it is stored, then it includes the action performed for traceability.
Given the audit trail exists, when queried, then logged actions are retrievable in the order they occurred.
Given an action fails to complete, when the failure occurs, then the system does not log it as a successful action.

Relates to S-008 (Additional requirements (R-015–R-019)): Audit log retention and access permissions fall under the secure-storage and RBAC work.

stories.userStory: As a system, I want to integrate with an email service, so that notifications and communications (e.g., welcome pack, reminders) can be delivered to users.

gaps.description: BRD does not specify what onboarding task types beyond documents/equipment/training make up the checklist, nor who creates/configures checklist templates.
gaps.clarificationQuestion: Who defines/configures the onboarding checklist items and due dates per new hire — is it HR-configurable per role/department, or a fixed template?

gaps.description: BRD does not specify what happens if a document upload fails validation (wrong format/size) - only that format/size limits exist.
gaps.clarificationQuestion: What error handling/user feedback is expected when a document upload fails validation?

gaps.description: BRD does not specify equipment request creation - only approval. Unclear who initiates equipment requests (new hire, manager, or auto-generated).
gaps.clarificationQuestion: Who initiates/creates the equipment request that the Manager approves?

gaps.description: BRD mentions 'training' as an onboarding task category in the objective but provides no functional requirements for training management.
gaps.clarificationQuestion: What training-related functionality, if any, is required for new hires beyond the general checklist?

gaps.description: BRD does not define what HRIS integration entails beyond 'employee records' - e.g., is it read-only sync, bidirectional, or triggers onboarding record creation?
gaps.clarificationQuestion: What data flows are required between the portal and HRIS (read-only lookup, write-back, real-time sync)?

gaps.description: BRD states reminders are sent by HR but does not specify trigger conditions (manual vs automatic based on due dates) or reminder channel.
gaps.clarificationQuestion: Are reminders manually triggered by HR, or should the system auto-trigger reminders based on approaching/overdue due dates?

gaps.description: BRD does not specify password policies or authentication details beyond SSO (e.g., session timeout, MFA) since SSO is delegated to Azure AD.

gaps.clarificationQuestion: Are there any authentication requirements beyond Azure AD SSO delegation (e.g., session timeout, MFA)?

gaps.description: No encryption/transport security standard (e.g., HTTPS/TLS) is stated for data in transit.
gaps.impact: Inferred best-practice / unstated item — not in the BRD; confirm whether it is in scope.

gaps.description: 'Documents stored securely' is unspecified — no encryption-at-rest standard, access control specifics, or storage location/provider named.
gaps.impact: Inferred best-practice / unstated item — not in the BRD; confirm whether it is in scope.
gaps.clarificationQuestion: What specific security controls (encryption at rest, access permissions, storage provider) define 'securely stored' documents?

gaps.description: No data retention or deletion policy stated for uploaded documents or audit logs.
gaps.impact: Inferred best-practice / unstated item — not in the BRD; confirm whether it is in scope.

gaps.description: No performance/response-time targets given beyond '200 concurrent new hires' (e.g., page load time, upload processing time).

gaps.description: No error-handling behavior specified for failed SSO login, failed document upload, or integration failures (Azure AD, email service, HRIS downtime).

gaps.description: No specification of what happens if a new hire misses a due date on the checklist (escalation, overdue flag).

gaps.description: No detail on equipment request initiation — who creates the equipment request before manager approval.

recommendedSprintStories: IT Account Provisioning on Equipment Approval
dependencyNotes: Email Service Integration must be completed before or alongside Automated Welcome Pack Email and HR Send Reminders to New Hires, as both rely on the email service.
IT Account Provisioning on Equipment Approval depends on the Manager equipment approval workflow (covered in R-001–R-013 SSO/access foundation and equipment request stories) being functional first.
System-Wide Audit Logging of Actions should be integrated early since HR Dashboard, IT Provisioning, and Reminders all need to emit audit events.
HR Dashboard for Onboarding Completion Tracking depends on New Hire checklist/task and document upload data being available, which are part of R-001–R-013/R-015–R-019 foundational stories.

Authentication & Access Control stories (R-001–R-013, R-015–R-019) are foundational (SSO, RBAC) and should be prioritized first since nearly all other stories assume an authenticated, role-based session.
riskSummary: SSO integration with Azure AD may surface unforeseen configuration or tenant-access issues, risking delays to all dependent stories.
Email Service Integration is a third-party dependency; outages or delayed vendor setup could block Welcome Pack and Reminder features.
Audit logging must capture actions across multiple stories being built in parallel; if implemented late, retrofitting logging into already-built features may require rework.
Concurrent load requirement (200 new hires) is not directly tested in this sprint and should be validated in a later performance-focused sprint.
Document storage security and HR notification-on-upload are not included in this sprint's story list, creating a scope gap risk if assumed complete.
Ambiguity remains around what exactly R-001–R-013 and R-015–R-019 cover since they are bundled 'additional requirements' rather than discrete stories, risking underestimation.
definitionOfReadyChecklist: User story has a clear, testable description and acceptance criteria
Dependencies (e.g., SSO, email service) identified and their availability confirmed
UI/UX designs or wireframes available where applicable (e.g., HR dashboard, checklist)
Azure AD SSO test tenant/credentials available for development and QA
Story sized and estimated by the team
Acceptance criteria reviewed and agreed upon by Product Owner
definitionOfDoneChecklist: Code developed, peer-reviewed, and merged to main branch
Unit and integration tests written and passing
Acceptance criteria fully met and verified by QA
Audit logging confirmed for all relevant actions in the story
Role-based access control verified for all applicable user roles
No critical or high-severity defects open
Documentation updated (technical and user-facing where applicable)
Story demoed to Product Owner and accepted
